title: Radiological Evaluation of Fracture Age Based on Tissue Samples
summary: In the reconstruction of crime scenes, the ability to estimate the age of a bone fracture is essential. The aim of this study is to document and categorize the appearance of bone fractures at different stages of healing using radiological methods. This will be carried out on tissue samples from deceased individuals
conditions: Bone fracture for which the age is to be determined.

interventions.name: The study is to be conducted on tissue samples from a maximum of 100 corpses, which are collected as part of the postmortem routine diagnostics at the Institute of Legal and Traffic Medicine of the University Hospital Heidelberg. After the request for an autopsy is made to the Institute of Legal Med

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- An autopsy request has been issued by the competent authority.
- Routine postmortem imaging is indicated and/or premortem images are available.
- Bone fractures are present that can be attributed to a dated traumatic event.
Exclusion criteria:
- No bone fractures are present.
- The timing of the trauma-inducing event is uncertain.
- No premortem images are available, and postmortem imaging is not indicated according to the indication catalogue of the Working Group on Forensic Imaging of the German Society of Legal Medicine.
- Advanced postmortem changes are present.
